title: Final Value of Variable After Performing Operations
summary: Given an array of strings representing operations on a variable X initialized to zero, return the final value of X after executing all operations.
statement: Given an array of strings representing operations on a variable X initialized to zero, return the final value of X after executing all operations. Operations include incrementing (X++ or ++X) and decrementing (X-- or --X) the variable by one.
constraints: operations has 1 through 100 strings, each one of ++X, X++, --X, or X--.
X starts at zero; increment operations add one and decrement operations subtract one.
Return X after applying operations in order.
reference_solution:
def final_variable_value(operations):
    value=0
    for operation in operations:value+=1 if '+' in operation else -1
    return value
known_wrong_solutions:
def final_variable_value(operations):
    value=0
    for operation in operations:value+=1 if operation=='++X' else -1
    return value
def final_variable_value(operations):
    value=1
    for operation in operations:value+=1 if '+' in operation else -1
    return value
hints: All four strings encode only the sign of a one-unit change.
Test whether the operation contains plus; otherwise it is a decrement.
Initialize zero and add +1 for plus operations or -1 for minus operations.
Applying the encoded change once per operation exactly simulates the variable, regardless of prefix or postfix notation.
editorial: Applying the encoded change once per operation exactly simulates the variable, regardless of prefix or postfix notation.

tests.explanation: The changes are minus one, plus one, plus one, ending at one.
Three increments leave X equal to three.
